title: Grow a Heap Buffer Without Dangling
hints: Run the starter and read the AddressSanitizer report. The first stack trace is the line that touched dead memory; `freed by thread T0 here` shows the `delete[]` that killed it. Which pointer is still being read after you deleted it?

The order is fixed: allocate the new block, copy the first `min(old_n, new_n)` values across, and only *then* `delete[] old`. `std::min` lives in `<algorithm>` and wants both arguments of the same type, so keep sizes as `std::size_t`.
